rationale: Lyc noun appearing twice on this page (lines 3, 26) in contexts requiring a sense of allotted share or accumulated credit. Line 3: 'let a ⲍⲏⲣ become in your life'; line 26: 'your toil shall be reckoned to your ⲍⲏⲣ.' Best parallel is Coptic ⲡⲱⲣ/ϩⲏⲣ register for 'lot, share, portion of recompense.' Tentative; confidence moderate.

Reduplicated Lyc verb appearing twice (lines 4, 5) as the negative behavior parallel to παραιτεῖσθαι 'refuse.' Possibly related to ⲡⲱϣⲡⲱϣ 'split, divide' (be divided in heart) or to a deficiency-verb. Captures the moral-paraenetic warning against laxity in the face of the church-building task. Tentative; confidence low.

Obscure Greek loanword (line 8) in series 'glory and kingship and ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲫⲟⲛ of the one who proclaims.' Possible candidates include παρρησία 'boldness, free-speech' (with corrupted spelling) or a παρα-φορ- compound denoting an honor or accompanying gift. Cannot identify with confidence.

Lyc reduplicated noun (line 21) governed by 'bear': ⲁⲃⲓ ⲡⲉϥⲣⲁⲣϣ̄ 'bear his burden.' Likely from Coptic ⲉⲣⲱϣⲉ/ⲣⲱϣ 'weight, load, care.' The reduplication may intensify ('heavy burden') or be dialectal feature.

Lyc article cluster ⲡⲣ̄- + ⲍⲱⲃ (= ϩⲱⲃ 'work,' already in glossary) functions as a single technical term denoting 'the (church-building) work.' Construction ⲣ̄-ⲡⲣ̄ⲍⲱⲃ 'do the work' is the controlling verbal idiom of this kephalaion (lines 2, 15, 22).

Lyc imperative idiom (line 24): ⲧⲧ from ⲧⲱⲧ 'turn/take' or possibly imperative of ϯ 'give'; with ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲕ̄ 'into your hand' = 'take into your hand' meaning 'undertake, assume responsibility for.' Standard Coptic verbal idiom for assuming a task.
